requirements.heading: Registration Requirements
requirements.text: New access type specifications MUST conform to the requirements described below.

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: Each access type MUST have a unique name.

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: This name appears in the access-type parameter in the message/external-body content-type header field and MUST conform to MIME content type parameter syntax.

requirements.heading: Mechanism Specification Requirements
requirements.text: All of the protocols, transports, and procedures used by a given access type MUST be described, either in the specification of the access type itself or in some other publicly available specification, in sufficient detail for the access type to be implemented by any competent implementor.

requirements.heading: Publication Requirements
requirements.text: All access types MUST be described by an RFC.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: Any known security issues that arise from the use of the access type MUST be completely and fully described.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: Additional security considerations SHOULD be addressed by publishing revised versions of the access type specification.

requirements.heading: Transfer Encoding Requirements
requirements.text: Transfer encoding specifications MUST conform to the requirements described below.

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: Each transfer encoding MUST have a unique name.

requirements.heading: Naming Requirements
requirements.text: This name appears in the Content-Transfer-Encoding header field and MUST conform to the syntax of that field.

requirements.heading: Algorithm Specification Requirements
requirements.text: All of the algorithms used in a transfer encoding (e.g., conversion to printable form, compression) MUST be described in their entirety in the transfer encoding specification.

requirements.heading: Algorithm Specification Requirements
requirements.text: The restrictions imposed by [RFC2026] on the standardization of patented algorithms MUST be respected as well.

requirements.heading: Input Domain Requirements
requirements.text: All transfer encodings MUST be applicable to an arbitrary sequence of octets of any length.

requirements.heading: Output Range Requirements
requirements.text: However, the output format for each transfer encoding MUST be fully and completely documented.

requirements.heading: Output Range Requirements
requirements.text: In particular, each specification MUST clearly state whether the output format always lies within the confines of 7bit or 8bit or is simply pure binary data.

requirements.heading: Data Integrity and Generality Requirements
requirements.text: All transfer encodings MUST be fully invertible on any platform; it MUST be possible for anyone to recover the original data by performing the corresponding decoding operation.

requirements.heading: New Functionality Requirements
requirements.text: All transfer encodings MUST provide some sort of new functionality.

requirements.heading: New Functionality Requirements
requirements.text: Some degree of functionality overlap with previously defined transfer encodings is acceptable, but any new transfer encoding MUST also offer something no other transfer encoding provides.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: To the greatest extent possible, transfer encodings SHOULD NOT contain known security issues.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: Regardless, any known security issues that arise from the use of the transfer encoding MUST be completely and fully described.

requirements.heading: Security Requirements
requirements.text: If additional security issues come to light after initial publication and registration, they SHOULD be addressed by publishing revised versions of the transfer encoding specification.

requirements.heading: Transfer Encoding Definition Procedure
requirements.text: The draft MUST define the transfer encoding precisely and completely, and it MUST also provide substantial justification for defining and standardizing a new transfer encoding.

requirements.heading: Transfer Encoding Definition Procedure
requirements.text: This specification MUST then be presented to the IESG for consideration.

requirements.heading: IANA Procedures for Transfer Encoding Registration
requirements.text: All legitimate transfer encoding registrations MUST appear as a standards-track RFC, so it is the IESG's responsibility to notify the IANA when a new transfer encoding has been approved.
